name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,707

clue.text: Festival date: around Saint Marina?

indicators.note: to sit around something is to surround it, so one piece goes outside another

blocks.note: to date someone is to court or woo them
a marina is a kind of dock for boats, hence the question mark
ST is the standard abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A festival day planned around Saint Marina, as if she were a patron saint being honoured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saint Marina' reads as one name, but the saint is tucked inside the marina. Woodstock is also Snoopy's little yellow bird friend, the first hint of a Peanuts theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodstock was the famous 1969 rock music gathering held on a farm in New York State.

clue.text: Stop burning counterfoil!

blocks.note: first meaning: to put out a cigarette by pressing its end down
second meaning: the part of a ticket or cheque kept as a record

explanation.surface: An urgent order to stop a counterfoil from going up in flames.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation makes it one command about saving a ticket; it splits into a verb for snuffing a cigarette and a noun for the kept part of a cheque.
explanation.definitionFit: You stub out a cigarette to extinguish it, and the retained half of a cheque book page is called its stub.

clue.text: Spying some typo on script returned

indicators.note: some means only part of what follows, so the letters sit inside a longer run
something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters are read right to left

blocks.note: the run of letters straddling the three words

explanation.surface: An editor catching a typo in a script that has been sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading 'typo on s' backwards gives SNOOPY, the beagle at the heart of this puzzle's Peanuts theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone snoopy pries into other people's business, which is much the same as being nosy and spying.

clue.text: Actors Kingsley and Courtenay, maybe, cycled to Bury

indicators.note: to cycle is to go round, so the letter at the front rides round to the back

blocks.note: the actor Sir Ben Kingsley
the actor Sir Tom Courtenay; 'maybe' flags that only the first name is wanted

explanation.surface: Two famous actors cycling to the Lancashire town of Bury.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is a town near Manchester, which makes it look like a destination; it is the verb. BENTOM with its first letter moved to the end gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To entomb a body is to place it in a tomb or grave, a formal synonym for burying it.

clue.text: Unruly boat user is one causing damage

indicators.note: something unruly will not stay in order, so these letters break ranks and rearrange

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rowdy person on a boat ends up wrecking things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unruly' seems to describe the boat user, but it tells you to rearrange those eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A saboteur deliberately wrecks equipment or plans, so is literally a person who does harm on purpose.

clue.text: Ancient Pope discovered in Roswell - in USA

indicators.note: something discovered in a place was found lying within it, so the letters are inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the town name and the next two words

explanation.surface: A tabloid-style tale of an ancient pope turning up at Roswell, New Mexico, famed for its alleged alien crash.
explanation.walkthrough: Roswell's UFO legend makes it a natural place for a strange discovery. Linus is also Charlie Brown's blanket-carrying friend in Peanuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Linus is traditionally counted as the second bishop of Rome, following Peter, in the first century.

clue.text: Revealing orientation of spin

blocks.note: first meaning: publicly exposing someone's sexuality
second meaning: a short trip or jaunt, as in a spin in the car

explanation.surface: Reads like a physics phrase about a spinning particle's orientation being revealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spin' suggests physics or PR, but here it is a drive for pleasure. 'Orientation' is sexual orientation.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposing someone as gay is called outing them, and a short pleasure trip is also called an outing.

clue.text: Searching internet possibly, looking for game

blocks.note: first meaning: browsing the web using Apple's Safari browser
second meaning: on an expedition to see or hunt wild animals

explanation.surface: Someone browsing the internet in search of a computer game to play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' looks like a video game; it is wild animals. 'Possibly' admits that Safari is only one browser among several.
explanation.definitionFit: Safari is Apple's web browser, and an African wildlife expedition to view or hunt animals is also a safari.

clue.text: City dismisses marketing fever

indicators.note: to dismiss is to send away, so some letters are sent out of the word

blocks.note: the capital of the Czech Republic
PR is public relations, the publicity side of marketing

explanation.surface: A city council sacks its marketing team in a fit of temper.
explanation.walkthrough: Take PR away from the front of PRAGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ague is an old word for a fever with shivering fits, especially the recurring kind caused by malaria.

clue.text: He has to pay young lady, coming out with rock

blocks.note: a deb (debutante) is a young woman coming out, making her formal entry into high society
a tor is a rocky peak, as on Dartmoor in England

explanation.surface: A man must pay for a young woman going out with a rock star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming out' is not a container or anagram signal but part of the description of a debutante, who comes out into society.
explanation.definitionFit: A debtor is a person who owes money, so he is the one obliged to settle up with a creditor.

clue.text: Wrecked hull on U-boat (not British) docking at port

indicators.note: not means without, so that letter is left out
to dock is to cut short, as with a tail, so the following letters are cut off
a wrecked thing is smashed apart, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, before trimming
B is the abbreviation for British
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wrecked submarine hull being brought into a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Docking at port' reads as mooring, but 'docking' cuts the following word from the vessel, and with British also gone only two letters of it remain for the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Honolulu, the capital of Hawaii, is a major harbour city on the island of Oahu, home to Pearl Harbor nearby.

clue.text: Republican playing silly, interrupting to propose amendment, for instance?

indicators.note: playing around with something means not leaving it as it was, so the letters are rearranged
to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so one part goes inside another

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican
taken as written
in British usage, to table a motion is to put it forward for discussion

explanation.surface: A Republican playing the fool and disrupting a proposal to amend the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Propose amendment' looks like one parliamentary phrase, but 'to propose' gives TABLE and 'amendment' starts the definition. Note that in the US, to table a motion means to shelve it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word a-mend-ment has three syllables, so it is an example of a three-syllable word.

clue.text: Setter's mother rises for leader at prayers

indicators.note: in a down clue, something that rises is read from bottom to top, so it runs backwards

blocks.note: the setter refers to themselves as I, and 'setter's' is I'M, short for I am
Ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: The crossword setter's mother stands up to lead the prayers.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Setter's' stands for 'is', so it gives I'M rather than a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: An imam is the person who leads worship in a mosque, standing before the congregation to direct their prayer.

clue.text: Changing hands: whiskey and soda?

indicators.note: the two hands are right and left, so changing hands means one swaps for the other

blocks.note: rye is whiskey distilled from rye grain

explanation.surface: A bar order of whiskey and soda passed from one hand to another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whiskey and soda' looks like one drink order, but 'and' separates wordplay from definition: R (right) in RYE becomes L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: Lye is a strong alkali, and caustic soda (sodium hydroxide) is the commonest example, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Sharp object's point grasped by young servant

indicators.note: what is grasped is held within a hand, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: at English public schools a fag was a junior boy who ran errands for a senior pupil
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A young servant gripping the tip of something sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'object' stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay. 'Point' is a compass point, not a tip.
explanation.definitionFit: A fang is a long pointed tooth, like a snake's or a wolf's, so it is a sharp thing.

clue.text: I led a riot: damaged column

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A protester confesses to leading a riot that damaged a column, perhaps Nelson's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Column' suggests a stone pillar wrecked by rioters, but it is a newspaper column.
explanation.definitionFit: An editorial is an opinion piece written for a newspaper, the kind of regular article called a column.

clue.text: Awful liar imprisoned by revolutionary prince

indicators.note: something awful is in a bad state, so the letters are mangled and rearranged
a prisoner is shut inside walls, so one piece is locked within another

blocks.note: taken as written
Che Guevara is the crossword's standard revolutionary

explanation.surface: A dreadful liar locked up by a revolutionary prince.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary prince' reads as one person, but the revolutionary is CHE and 'prince' is the definition. Charlie Brown is the hero of Peanuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Edward Stuart, the Jacobite claimant to the British throne, is known as Bonnie Prince Charlie.

clue.text: Glass vase broken, son dropped here, you bet!

indicators.note: something dropped is let go, so that letter is left out
a broken thing is in pieces, so the letters are reassembled in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Someone's son knocked over a glass vase and broke it here, you can be sure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You bet!' sounds like an exclamation of agreement, but read literally it says this is the place where you gamble.
explanation.definitionFit: Las Vegas in Nevada is the world's best-known gambling city, full of casinos where visitors place wagers.

clue.text: See 29
Restrain the first man to lose his head

indicators.note: losing one's head means losing the top, so the opening letter is removed

blocks.note: in the Bible, Adam is the first man God created

explanation.surface: An order to hold back the first man before he is beheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the A from the front of ADAM.
explanation.definitionFit: To dam a river is to hold back its water with a barrier, so the verb means to check or hold in.

clue.text: See 29
Juliet isn't there to nudge Romeo: he's a stable chap

indicators.note: what isn't there is absent, so that letter is missing

blocks.note: J is Juliet in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to jostle is to push or nudge
R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: With Juliet away, Romeo is left to nudge along steadily, being a reliable sort.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo and Juliet suggest Shakespeare, but they are radio-alphabet letters. 'Stable' looks like 'steady'; it is a place for horses.
explanation.definitionFit: An ostler was the man who looked after travellers' horses at an inn, so he worked in the stables.

clue.text: Cardinal uses ancient entry occasionally

indicators.note: occasionally means every so often, so only letters at regular gaps are kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on

explanation.surface: A cardinal of the Church using an old doorway now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' suggests a churchman, but it means a cardinal number, one used for counting.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal numbers are the counting numbers, one, two, three and so on, and ninety is one of them.

clue.text: Shade upper part of face and tip of nose

indicators.note: a tip is an extreme end, so just the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: the brow is the forehead
the opening letter

explanation.surface: Shading the forehead and nose tip, as in a portrait drawing or against the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shade' looks like a verb for covering the face; it is a colour, and the answer completes Charlie Brown from 17 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Brown is a colour, and a shade is a particular colour or tone of one.

clue.text: Girl is terribly clumsy, having mislaid manuscript

indicators.note: what has been mislaid is lost, so those letters are missing
doing something terribly means doing it badly, so the letters come out jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript

explanation.surface: A girl who is so clumsy she has lost her manuscript.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove M and S from CLUMSY and rearrange what is left. Lucy is Linus's bossy sister in Peanuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucy is a common female first name, and crosswords often clue any such name simply by its sex.

clue.text: Have a wager with this Mutant Turtle with outsize shell

indicators.note: a mutant has changed form, so the letters take a new arrangement
a shell is an outer casing, so only the outside letters are kept

blocks.note: taken as written
the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Betting on one of the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles with an oversized shell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mutant Turtle' calls up the cartoon heroes, but 'Mutant' is the anagram signal, and 'shell' keeps only the outer letters of 'outsize'.
explanation.definitionFit: Roulette is a casino game where gamblers stake money on where a ball lands on a spinning numbered wheel.

clue.text: Fully clothed is perhaps what you need to be, to travel ...

definitions.text: what you need to be, to travel

blocks.note: first meaning: wearing one's gear, or kit

blocks.clueFragment: what you need to be, to travel
blocks.note: second meaning: a car must have a gear engaged before it can move

explanation.surface: Advice that you should be properly dressed before setting off on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing dots carry the thought into 28 across, which describes a traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear is informal for clothes or kit, and a vehicle moves only when its transmission is engaged.

clue.text: Raising dead besides others

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising lifts the letters upward, so they are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the late someone is someone who has died

explanation.surface: Raising the dead alongside other people, like a horror film resurrection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raising dead' sounds like resurrection; in a down clue it turns LATE upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Et al is the Latin abbreviation for et alii, meaning and others, used after a list of names.

clue.text: ... like this person, weary, shattered, covering a great distance

indicators.note: something shattered is in fragments, so the letters are pieced together differently
to cover something is to go around it, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: taken as written
far means a long way

explanation.surface: Continuing 26: a tired, exhausted walker who has come a very long way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weary, shattered' reads as two words for tiredness, but 'shattered' is the anagram signal. In British English, shattered also means exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: A wayfarer is a traveller on foot, the person the preceding clue describes setting off to travel.

clue.text: Unfortunately, this isn’t a grand way to mark dramatic opening

annotation.answer: IT WAS A DARK AND STORMY NIGHT

definitions.text: Unfortunately, this isn’t a grand way to mark dramatic opening

indicators.note: something unfortunate has gone wrong, so the letters fall into a different order
an opening is the start of something, so only the first letter is taken

blocks.clueFragment: this isn’t a grand way to mark
blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter

explanation.surface: A critic complaining that this is a poor way to begin a dramatic story.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition. The line, from Bulwer-Lytton's 1830 novel Paul Clifford, is a byword for overwrought prose, and Snoopy begins every novel he types with it.
explanation.definitionFit: This notoriously purple first sentence is the classic example of a melodramatic novel opening that falls flat.
